clue.text: Jade is last seen in Senegal

indicators.note: the word for last is seen sitting inside the abbreviation, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SN is the international country code for Senegal
latter means the last of two mentioned

explanation.surface: A green gemstone was last spotted somewhere in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' looks like the green stone but is an old insult for a disreputable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is an archaic term of abuse for a slovenly or loose woman, a synonym of slattern.

clue.text: Sad and angry about doctor

indicators.note: the word for angry goes round the doctor's letters, so it surrounds them

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast and cross with their physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means gloomy or melancholy, a close synonym of sad.

clue.text: Painter upset shelf of booze

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the painter's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock painter
a rack is a framework or shelf for holding things

explanation.surface: An artist knocks over a drinks shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrack is a strong Asian spirit distilled from palm sap or rice, so an example of booze.

clue.text: Ploughman makes lines in a row

definitions.text: Ploughman makes lines in a row

parts.words: Ploughman makes lines in a row
parts.note: one who tills the soil cuts furrows, lines laid side by side in rows across a field

explanation.surface: A farmer ploughs neat parallel furrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tills land is a cultivator or ploughman, whose work leaves parallel furrows.

clue.text: Authoritarian breaks instrument that's not for the public

indicators.note: the word for authoritarian breaks into the instrument, splitting it open

parts.note: a reed is a wind instrument, or a pipe made from one
strict means stern and authoritarian in discipline

explanation.surface: A dictator smashes a musical instrument kept from public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricted documents or areas are limited to authorised people, closed to general access.

clue.text: German admitting the object is sex

indicators.note: letting in, so the abbreviation for German takes the object inside it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, the object of an action

explanation.surface: A German confesses that the point of it all is sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is the grammatical or social category of sex, male or female.

clue.text: Look in skip for piece of meat

indicators.note: the word for look is placed in the word for skip

parts.note: to skip is to abscond or escape
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a builder's skip and finds some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip' looks like the rubbish container, but it is the verb meaning flee.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, flattened and fried.

clue.text: The state of the French pottery

parts.note: de la is French for of the, before a feminine noun
ware is ceramic goods, as in earthenware

explanation.surface: Condition of the pots made in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty United States, on the east coast.

clue.text: Diffident soldier was adequate

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, standing for a soldier
served means did well enough, as in it served its purpose

explanation.surface: A shy soldier did his duty well enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means restrained and slow to reveal feelings, much like diffident or shy.

clue.text: Fret about exam for puritan

indicators.note: the word for fret goes round the exam, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist on the coast of north-east England
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A strait-laced student worries over a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like the verb worry, but it is the noun for a coastal sea fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist preaches strict standards of conduct, as a puritan does.

clue.text: Bob picks boat race

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
culls means selects or picks out

explanation.surface: Someone named Bob chooses which regatta to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the pre-1971 British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculls is a rowing race for single scullers, such as the Diamond Sculls at Henley.

clue.text: Stun English judge of propulsion study

parts.note: to rock is to shock or stun
to try a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: An English judge is stunned by a lesson on propulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and engineering of rocket propulsion.

clue.text: Good bottom induces a stare

parts.note: lower means nearer the bottom, the underneath one

explanation.surface: A fine backside gets people gawping.
explanation.definitionFit: A glower is an angry, sullen stare or scowl.

clue.text: Teams become confused when not sitting up straight

parts.note: sides are opposing teams in a game
to addle is to become muddled or confused

explanation.surface: Teams get muddled when slouching in their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become confused' looks like an anagram signal, but it is simply the synonym that supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle means sitting with both legs on one side of the horse, rather than squarely astride.

clue.text: Dog for lively king in Kent

indicators.note: the lively word and the king are placed in the letters for Kent

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, so SE
chipper means cheerful and lively
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A dog is chosen for a lively monarch living in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT is a county in south-east England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A schipperke is a small black Belgian breed of dog, once used on barges.

clue.text: Platform for a couple of fellows in lecture

indicators.note: the a and two fellows go in the word for lecture

parts.note: to scold is to lecture or reprimand
F is fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A stage built for two academics giving a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, for builders or historically for executions.

clue.text: Engage virgin without hesitation

indicators.note: here means outside, so the virgin word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: intact means untouched or virgin
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a novice without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to engage with one another, act on each other.

clue.text: Publish record on waste

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the record comes first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose is to waste, as in lose an opportunity

explanation.surface: A recording is put out on a waste of vinyl.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal or make public, so to publish information.

clue.text: Thought to be against partiality of the left

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
side means a partisan faction or position favoured
red describes a left-wing socialist

explanation.surface: Thought to be against the bias of left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered means thought about carefully, or judged and regarded.

clue.text: Marina's tipsy pilot

indicators.note: something tipsy reels about, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the 's means is, so only the name gives letters

explanation.surface: Marina has had too much to drink and is the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a member of an air force, especially a pilot of aircraft.

clue.text: Rummage about for article in the smithy

indicators.note: the article is placed in the word for smithy

parts.note: a forge is a blacksmith's workshop
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone rummages around a blacksmith's shop for an object.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search widely for food or supplies, to rummage about.

clue.text: Rugby game is drawn in southern Sweden

indicators.note: the word for drawn is set in the two letters

parts.note: S is Sweden's international vehicle code
even means level, as in a drawn match

explanation.surface: A rugby match ends drawn in the south of Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a form of rugby union played with seven players a side.

clue.text: Leave church in warm clothing

parts.note: to flee is to leave hurriedly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of church wrapped up warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a soft warm jacket or top made of synthetic pile.

clue.text: Old king keeps writer in clothing

indicators.note: holds within, so the old king's name contains the writer

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch keeps an author in clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's light sleeveless undergarment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: One addressing other ranks has register back to front

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, enlisted soldiers

indicators.note: the word for register is read in reverse order

parts.note: a rota is a list or register of duties

explanation.surface: Someone talks to the troops holding the duty list the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, one who addresses an audience.

clue.text: A hindrance to marketing of water

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that holds back water
a sale is the act of selling, or marketing

explanation.surface: An obstacle to selling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: Director eats the stew

indicators.note: takes in, so the director's abbreviation contains the next word

explanation.surface: A film director tucks into the casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like a dish, but is the noun for agitation, as in 'in a stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a dither or in a stew is to be flustered and agitated.

clue.text: Ill temper of old queen in trouble

indicators.note: the old queen is placed in the word for trouble

parts.note: a mess is a troublesome situation
Queen Anne reigned 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A long-dead monarch in difficulty is in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness can be spitefulness or unkindness, a nasty or ill-tempered disposition.
